title: Changelog
summary: Chronological record of the printer software work now captured in the repository.

content.text: Plain summary
Owner-reviewed interface correction

The first production UI proposal replaced the printer's familiar screen and hid most Mainsail controls. The owner rejected that large simplification. The corrected candidate preserves complete upstream Mainsail and the exact stock Comgrow serial-TFT layout, with a constrained gateway enforcing the reviewed backend behavior.

The project moved from ad hoc printer setup and file fixes into a versioned, reviewable firmware and workflow package. The live printer stayed stock while the candidate was prepared and tested locally.
Printer setup and early print findings
OrcaSlicer was set up with stock T300 profiles, then refined for safer macro-owned startup behavior.
A Benchy printed successfully before first-layer testing.
First-layer tests showed uniform gaps between lines, strong bed adhesion, and likely bed/mesh/flow interactions rather than a single obvious Z-only problem.
A missing-sheet homing accident made plate-presence defense a hard requirement.
The nozzle appeared visually undamaged, while the bed had a small puncture.
Community macro and runtime work
GerGo gantry-leveling was kept as the selected private workflow and protected from public redistribution.
KAMP research led to using Smart Park and Line Purge concepts, with adaptive meshing held back because the stock bed range remained too large.
Factory corner purge and unsafe slicer startup were replaced in design by firmware-owned lifecycle macros.
End and cancel parking were redesigned to lift first and avoid lowering the head.
Timelapse support was bounded so camera/storage failure cannot affect print safety.
Mainline migration package
Pinned stack.lock.json records sources, versions, commits, hashes, and licenses.
Recovery and imaging tooling was added for eMMC capture, verification, write guards, and transfer safety.
Production and maintenance config trees were separated.
Safety policy, G-code admission scanning, Klipper extra, lifecycle macros, host service units, and UI defaults were added.
Full documentation, handover, audits, and release gates were added.
GitHub publication
The full public printer project was committed as 0590c50 Add T300 mainline migration candidate and pushed to GitHub origin/main after rebasing on the upstream t300-link documentation change.
Firmware and Orca refinement candidate

Added admitted-print-only pressure advance from 0 through 0.20, with strict parameter validation and cleanup resets. A paused admitted print can issue only the zero reset so cancellation still completes. Adaptive pressure advance and uploaded TUNING_TOWER remain disabled.
Removed the generic 5 mm stationary extrusion allowance and replaced it with consumed retraction credit plus tiny, audited Orca numeric-rounding tolerances.
Added the read-only Printer Status action. The current Klipper command is PRINTER_STATUS, which is visible in Mainsail and is the only operator macro shown on the stock touchscreen Macro page.
Added portable Orca 2.4.2 machine, filament, and process profiles, including zero-hop default and separate 0.4 mm collision-clearance variants.

Staged editable first-layer, orange bracket, and two Frieren review projects. No final G-code was delivered, and every necessary placeholder filament value remains visibly calibration-required rather than accepted.

Validated the candidate with 338 repository tests, 29 exact Klipper v0.13 production cases, one exact private-maintenance configuration load, 11 vendor Klipper v0.12 cases, exact Orca 2.4.2 normal slices, calibration-command contract tests, and a stage-bound large-format digital print.

Transcribed and researched the hull/floor-line tutorial against OrcaSlicer pull request 8107, Prusa's Benchy investigation, and Orca's setting documentation. Added a warn-first model review rule, flagged the camera bracket's base transition and inherited 25 percent overlap for owner review, and left both bracket and Frieren settings unchanged.
Recovery preflight and v14 candidate

Read-only live inspection confirmed the stock eMMC/USB layout and old eMMC-first U-Boot behavior. The selected recovery route is now an owner-operated 1,500,000-baud serial console and the ordinary U-Boot USB command; kexec is not the primary plan.
Added locked recovery boot hashes, an offline media auditor, a no-automation serial helper, exact Armbian identity correction, and matching laptop/recovery-agent eMMC identity checks.

Built owner-local commissioning stage v14 with the exact purchased GerGo package confined to maintenance mode. Its one reviewed Z-stepper release command is allowed only in that private attended configuration; production G-code still forbids motor-release commands.
The final offline validation report passed all eleven checks, including the exact v14 stage, both Klipper versions, UI/services, secret scan, and a near-full-build-volume synthetic print.
Stock touchscreen gateway and v21 candidate

Discarded the replacement KlipperScreen interface after owner review. The candidate now preserves the exact Comgrow serial-TFT firmware, artwork, navigation, file browser, print screen, manual movement, temperature controls, and persistent Emergency Stop.

Placed the proprietary bridge behind an unprivileged loopback compatibility gateway. The bridge has serial-TFT access but no raw GPIO, shell, updater, configuration-write, unrestricted Moonraker, or service-restart authority. Its first hidden startup FIRMWARE_RESTART is acknowledged without restarting Klipper; later explicit restart buttons retain their advertised behavior.

Audited all 77 known stock controls. Each is classified as preserved, translated, local, constrained, or explicitly refused. The Macro page now shows only read-only Printer Status; Pause, Resume, Stop, and Change Filament remain in their dedicated stock locations.

Hardened homing state: successful X/Y-only homing does not move Z and preserves plate readiness, while any failed home stops in Klipper error and clears plate readiness. Z-only and all-axis touchscreen homing require prior plate confirmation in Mainsail because the stock TFT cannot render the checkbox.

Set production Klipper service crash behavior to Restart=no. A real Klippy process crash therefore remains down for inspection instead of creating an unexplained automatic recovery cycle; ordinary explicit restart commands still work while Klipper is responsive.

Built owner-local commissioning stage v21. It passed 373 repository tests, 34 exact Klipper v0.13 production cases, 11 vendor Klipper v0.12 cases, private maintenance configuration loading, the exact touchscreen contract, policy and secret checks, and the 900-layer near-full-volume digital print. The stage remains commissioning-only until the control-disabled USB boot and attended hardware tests pass.
